MASTER BUILD PROMPT — ARENA STUDIO

1. ROLE AND MISSION

You are acting as a senior software architect, lead React Native engineer, UI/UX designer, DevOps engineer and AI agent systems developer.

Your task is to build ARENA STUDIO.

ARENA STUDIO is a professional mobile-first application development environment designed primarily for iPhone.

It combines:

* A mobile IDE.
* An application project manager.
* Live iOS application previews.
* An AI agent management system.
* A custom skills library.
* Multi-agent task orchestration.
* Design and asset management.
* Build and deployment management.
* Arena.ai integration.

This must become a real, functional application.

Do not build a static prototype, a mock dashboard or a collection of disconnected screens.

Build the application incrementally, with working navigation, persistent data, functional controls and a maintainable architecture.

2. EXISTING ENVIRONMENT — IMPORTANT

The application is being developed using:

* Expo.
* React Native.
* TypeScript.
* Expo Go on a physical iPhone.
* Google Antigravity as the development IDE.

IMPORTANT:

First inspect the existing repository.

Do not delete or overwrite existing working functionality without understanding it.

Do not create a second Expo project unnecessarily.

Preserve the existing project configuration wherever possible.

Ensure the initial implementation works in Expo Go.

Features requiring native modules unavailable in Expo Go must be isolated and documented for a later development build.

The development computer will run the Metro development server and build tooling. The iPhone will act as the primary application interface and preview device.

3. PRODUCT IDENTITY

Product name: ARENA STUDIO

Tagline: Build. Design. Develop. Deploy.

Visual direction:

Professional developer software with a premium dark interface.

Avoid:

* Excessive AI-themed graphics.
* Overused glowing gradients.
* Futuristic science-fiction dashboards.
* Excessive glassmorphism.
* Oversized decorative cards.
* Unnecessary animations.

Use:

* Graphite and charcoal backgrounds.
* White and muted grey typography.
* Restrained blue and violet accents.
* Clear hierarchy.
* Carefully designed cards.
* Professional developer-tool styling.
* Subtle animations and haptic feedback.
* Native-feeling iOS interactions.

Design references:

* Xcode for development structure.
* VS Code for coding functionality.
* Linear for project management.
* Apple’s native design language for interactions.

The application should feel like a serious professional development product.

4. MAIN APPLICATION NAVIGATION

Create a persistent bottom navigation with:

1. Home
2. Projects
3. IDE
4. Agents
5. Tools

Deploy should be accessible from the project workspace and build management area.

The interface must adapt to different iPhone screen sizes.

Use safe areas and proper keyboard handling.

5. PHASE ONE — DESIGN SYSTEM

Before building screens, establish a reusable design system.

Create:

* Colour tokens.
* Typography scale.
* Spacing system.
* Border radius system.
* Shadows.
* Icon system.
* Button components.
* Input components.
* Cards.
* Modal components.
* Bottom sheets.
* Navigation components.
* Loading states.
* Empty states.
* Error states.
* Status badges.

Use reusable components rather than duplicating styles.

Create a consistent application theme.

Support dark mode initially, with architecture allowing light mode later.

Deliverable:
A complete reusable UI component library.

6. PHASE TWO — HOME DASHBOARD

Create the ARENA STUDIO home screen.

Include:

* ARENA STUDIO branding.
* User profile.
* Notifications.
* New project action.
* Recent projects.
* Project status.
* Recent activity.
* Quick-start templates.
* Agent activity summary.
* Running workflows.
* Quick access to the IDE.

Project cards should show:

* Project name.
* Project type.
* Framework.
* Last modified.
* Build status.
* Preview availability.
* Quick actions.

Include example projects:

* NEXA Finance.
* Arena Browser.
* BOTWORKS.

These are demonstration projects and must be clearly distinguishable from actual imported projects.

Deliverable:
A functional home dashboard with project navigation.

7. PHASE THREE — PROJECT MANAGEMENT

Create a project management system.

Users must be able to:

* Create projects.
* Rename projects.
* Delete projects with confirmation.
* Duplicate project records.
* Import project information.
* Assign projects to categories.
* Set project descriptions.
* Select frameworks.
* View project activity.
* Manage project settings.

Initial project types:

* Expo / React Native.
* iOS.
* Web.
* React.
* Next.js.
* Game development.

Create a project details screen with tabs:

* Overview.
* Files.
* Activity.
* Agents.
* Settings.

Persist project metadata locally.

Never pretend a project has been imported unless its files have actually been imported.

8. PHASE FOUR — THE IDE

Build a proper mobile-first development workspace.

Required functionality:

File explorer

* Nested folders.
* File listing.
* File creation.
* Folder creation.
* Rename.
* Delete.
* Search.
* File selection.

Code editor

* Syntax highlighting.
* Line numbers.
* Search within files.
* Multiple open tabs.
* Unsaved change indicators.
* Save functionality.
* Basic editing operations.
* Error highlighting where supported.

Use an appropriate editor implementation compatible with the chosen runtime.

Investigate CodeMirror or Monaco-based approaches.

Do not assume desktop Monaco works correctly in React Native without testing.

Developer tools

* Git status.
* Branch information.
* Change summaries.
* Terminal interface.
* Build logs.
* Error logs.

A terminal interface must not pretend commands have executed unless connected to an actual execution environment.

For the first release, support editing project files through a properly connected development backend or supported local project mechanism.

Deliverable:
A working mobile development workspace.

9. PHASE FIVE — LIVE IOS PREVIEW

This is one of the most important features.

The user must be able to develop an Expo application on their computer and preview it on their iPhone.

Architecture:

Development computer:

* Project files.
* Node.js.
* Expo CLI.
* Metro bundler.
* Development server.

iPhone:

* ARENA STUDIO.
* Expo Go.
* Project preview interface.

Implement:

* Development server connection status.
* Project preview selection.
* Device information.
* Refresh preview.
* Open in Expo Go.
* Development error display.
* Connection diagnostics.
* Build logs.

Clearly distinguish between:

* Expo Go preview.
* Custom development builds.
* Production builds.

Do not display a connected state unless a real connection has been established.

Investigate the most reliable way to launch and manage an Expo preview from the mobile application.

10. PHASE SIX — AGENT CENTRE

This is a defining feature of ARENA STUDIO.

Build a full AI agent management environment.

Agents must be represented as specialist team members.

Create initial agent templates:

1. Architect Agent.
2. Developer Agent.
3. Design Agent.
4. Research Agent.
5. QA Agent.
6. Release Agent.
7. Documentation Agent.
8. 3D Design Agent.

Every agent must have:

* Name.
* Description.
* Role.
* Instructions.
* Assigned skills.
* Available tools.
* Permissions.
* Project access.
* Current task.
* Current status.
* Activity history.
* Execution settings.

Agent statuses:

* Idle.
* Ready.
* Working.
* Waiting.
* Paused.
* Failed.
* Completed.

Create an agent management screen with:

* Active agents.
* Agent library.
* Create agent.
* Edit agent.
* Assign skills.
* Assign tasks.
* Pause execution.
* Resume execution.
* View activity.
* View logs.

Users must be able to create their own agents.

An agent should have configurable instructions and specialist capabilities.

11. PHASE SEVEN — SKILLS LIBRARY

Create a reusable skills management system.

Skills are capabilities that can be assigned to agents.

Create categories:

DEVELOPMENT:

* React Native.
* Expo.
* TypeScript.
* JavaScript.
* Python.
* API Integration.
* Git and GitHub.
* Database Development.

DESIGN:

* UI Design.
* UX Research.
* Design Systems.
* Graphic Design.
* Image Generation.
* Blender.
* 3D Modelling.

TESTING:

* Unit Testing.
* Integration Testing.
* Debugging.
* Performance Testing.
* Accessibility Testing.

OPERATIONS:

* Deployment.
* CI/CD.
* Vercel.
* EAS Build.
* Release Management.

Users must be able to:

* Browse skills.
* Search skills.
* Create custom skills.
* Edit skills.
* Delete skills.
* Assign skills to agents.
* Remove skills from agents.
* View which agents use each skill.

A skill must have:

* Name.
* Description.
* Category.
* Instructions.
* Required tools.
* Version.
* Assigned agents.

Skills must be stored persistently.

Do not claim that a skill is executable simply because its description exists. Connect it to an actual supported agent execution system.

12. PHASE EIGHT — MULTI-AGENT ORCHESTRATION

Build a task orchestration engine.

Users must be able to provide a project objective.

Example:

“Build a personal finance application.”

The system should support:

1. Architect creates a project plan.
2. Designer prepares the UI specification.
3. Developer implements the application.
4. QA tests the application.
5. Release Agent prepares deployment.

Create:

* Task queue.
* Task priorities.
* Task dependencies.
* Agent assignment.
* Execution status.
* Progress tracking.
* Activity timeline.
* Task cancellation.
* Retry handling.
* Human approval checkpoints.

Support parallel execution when dependencies permit.

Create a workflow visualisation showing which agents are working, what they are doing and which tasks are waiting.

IMPORTANT:

Implement the orchestration engine separately from the visual interface.

Use real execution states when connected to an execution backend.

Use clearly labelled demonstration data when no execution backend is connected.

Do not simulate successful AI execution.

13. PHASE NINE — ARENA.AI INTEGRATION

Arena.ai is an existing website and account that the user wants to use.

The initial integration must preserve the real Arena website experience.

Implement a dedicated Arena workspace using react-native-webview.

Requirements:

* Load the actual Arena website.
* Allow the user to authenticate directly.
* Preserve website session data where supported.
* Support navigation.
* Support conversation usage.
* Allow users to interact with Arena’s real chat interface.
* Provide a way to return to ARENA STUDIO.

Do not collect or store Arena passwords.

Do not reverse-engineer private endpoints.

Investigate officially supported APIs, integrations and agent capabilities before implementing deeper automation.

The application must distinguish between:

* Native ARENA STUDIO agents.
* Arena.ai website functionality.
* Officially connected external agent capabilities.

Do not claim that the app can control Arena’s private internal agent system without an officially supported integration.

14. PHASE TEN — DESIGN STUDIO

Create a design workspace for application development.

Include:

* Design tokens.
* Colour palettes.
* Typography.
* Components.
* Component previews.
* Reusable templates.
* Asset library.
* Icons.
* Image resources.
* Design notes.

Allow users to create and organise design assets.

Connect generated assets to the selected project.

15. PHASE ELEVEN — TOOLS AND INTEGRATIONS

Create a tools and integrations management area.

Potential integrations:

* GitHub.
* Vercel.
* Supabase.
* Expo.
* EAS.
* Google Drive.

Include:

* Connection status.
* Authentication status.
* Permissions.
* Disconnect functionality.
* Integration settings.

Never store sensitive tokens in plaintext application storage.

16. PHASE TWELVE — BUILD AND DEPLOY

Create a dedicated deployment workspace.

Support:

* Expo build preparation.
* EAS Build integration.
* iOS build configuration.
* TestFlight preparation.
* App Store release preparation.
* Web deployment through Vercel.
* Build history.
* Release history.
* Deployment logs.
* Error reporting.

Deployment must require explicit user confirmation.

Do not report a build or deployment as successful until the relevant service confirms success.

Clearly display:

* Development.
* Preview.
* Production.

17. DATA ARCHITECTURE

Design a scalable data model.

Core entities:

* Users.
* Projects.
* ProjectFiles.
* Agents.
* Skills.
* AgentSkills.
* Tasks.
* TaskDependencies.
* Workflows.
* WorkflowRuns.
* AgentActivity.
* Integrations.
* BuildJobs.
* Deployments.
* DesignAssets.

Use local persistence for the initial prototype.

Prepare a clean abstraction for a future Supabase backend.

Keep the data layer separate from UI components.

18. PHASE THIRTEEN — TESTING AND VALIDATION

Test every important interaction.

Test:

* Navigation.
* Project creation.
* Project editing.
* Persistence.
* Agent creation.
* Skill assignment.
* Task assignment.
* Workflow dependencies.
* Status changes.
* Arena WebView.
* Preview connection.
* Error handling.
* Screen responsiveness.
* Keyboard handling.
* App restart behaviour.

Do not invent test results.

Report:

* Passed.
* Failed.
* Not tested.
* Blocked by missing integration.

Fix errors before moving to the next major phase.

19. DEVELOPMENT PROCESS

Work in the following order:

PHASE A: Inspect the existing repository and report its structure.

PHASE B: Establish the design system and application architecture.

PHASE C: Build navigation and the Home dashboard.

PHASE D: Build project management.

PHASE E: Build the IDE interface.

PHASE F: Build Expo preview integration.

PHASE G: Build Agents.

PHASE H: Build Skills.

PHASE I: Build Workflows and orchestration.

PHASE J: Integrate Arena.ai.

PHASE K: Build Design Studio.

PHASE L: Build Integrations.

PHASE M: Build Deploy.

PHASE N: Test and optimise the complete application.

At the end of each phase:

1. Explain what was implemented.
2. List files created or modified.
3. Report which features actually work.
4. Report anything still mocked or awaiting integration.
5. Run relevant tests.
6. Fix errors.
7. Provide instructions for testing on the physical iPhone.

Do not skip phases.

Do not rewrite the entire project in one operation.

Do not introduce unnecessary dependencies.

Maintain readable, modular and documented code.

20. FINAL PRODUCT STANDARD

The finished product should feel like a professional mobile development environment.

It should allow the user to:

* Manage multiple software projects.
* Edit application code.
* Preview applications on an iPhone.
* Create specialist agents.
* Assign reusable skills.
* Coordinate multiple agents.
* Monitor tasks.
* Organise design assets.
* Use Arena.ai.
* Build and deploy applications.

The most important product principle:

THE USER IS THE PROJECT MANAGER.

The agents are the development team.

ARENA STUDIO is the environment connecting everything.

Begin with PHASE A.

Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

Do not proceed directly to implementation until you have reported the repository structure, existing dependencies, Expo compatibility and recommended architecture.
Spin up 20 agent to build this at the same time
